# Collapsible — M3 guidance

<!-- Generated by apps/site/scripts/one-off/migrate-guidance.mjs. Do not edit by hand.
     The component pages carry the reference; this file carries the guidance. -->

## Web

### Features

Reach for a collapsible when some of the content is optional reading: the details behind a summary, the advanced settings under a form, the rest of a long list. The trigger is the contract — what it says must describe what opens, and its state must be visible. Keep the thing that opens self-contained; a collapsible whose content needs the context above it has just hidden something important. If everything should be open all the time, do not build the toggle. If the content is navigation, that is a disclosure in a menu, not a collapsible.

### Anatomy

| Part | Role |
| --- | --- |
| CollapsibleRoot | Owns the open state. Accepts `open`/`onOpenChange` to control it. |
| CollapsibleTrigger | What opens it. Carries the expanded state, so its meaning is announced rather than implied by an arrow rotating. |
| CollapsiblePanel | The revealed content. Kept out of the tab order while closed. |
| Collapsible | The namespace object: Root, Trigger and Panel. |

## Native

### Features

Reach for a collapsible when a single block of content is optional to the task in front of the reader: advanced options, a legal footnote, the detail behind a summary. The title is a prop and the content is children, so the trigger layout stays the accordion's sibling's — and stays consistent — while what is revealed is entirely yours. Open state is the usual controlled-uncontrolled pair, and the content is unmounted while closed rather than hidden.
